US AI is generating far more revenue than Chinese AI:

As of the end of September, OpenAI and Anthropic had a combined estimated annualized revenue run rate of $105 billion.

This is nearly 10 times the $11 billion generated by 6 Chinese AI companies, including Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek, Z Dot ai, Moonshot AI, and MiniMax.

ByteDance accounted for 36% of this figure at $4 billion.

In Q3 alone, Anthropic's sales grew +47% QoQ, to a record $17 billion.

At the same time, OpenAI revenue surged +50% to a record $10 billion.

By comparison, DeepSeek's annualized revenue run rate doubled in September, but stands at just $1 billion.

US tech firms remain in the lead of the AI race.

Investor positioning in silver is experiencing violent swings:

Speculative investors sold -$2.3 billion in silver futures over the 5 weeks ending November 3rd, according to CFTC data.

This was driven by -$2.6 billion in new short positions, partially offset by +$300 million in new longs.

Hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), alongside smaller traders such as retail investors, accounted for most of the sales, with each group reducing exposure to silver futures by ~$1.4 billion.

As a result, aggregate net long speculative positioning fell to +$8.0 billion, its lowest since January 2025.

Since its January 2026 peak, this figure has dropped by more than -$16.0 billion.

Are investors overly bearish on silver?

One potential upside to a slowdown in the capex cycle is that it may put the Mag7 back in favor. We can see below that the P/E ratio of the M7 has diverged considerably from the P/PO (payout) multiple, ever since the M7 started spending their cashflows on capex instead of buybacks. As the payout ratio (dividends plus buybacks as a percentage of earnings) started falling from 90% to 29%, the P/E-multiple declined accordingly. My math suggests that if this had not happened, the Mag 7 could be trading at twice their current multiple. Between strength in the broader tape and this possible outcome, I could see a scenario in which the bull market (both cyclical and secular) can keep going, even without help from the AI picks and shovels.

US small businesses are signaling more inflation ahead:

The proportion of US small firms planning to raise prices over the next 3 months rose +6 percentage points in October, to 37%, the most since July 2022.

Excluding the post-pandemic surge in 2021 and 2022, this marks the highest reading since 2008.

By comparison, this figure did not exceed 30% between 2009 and 2019.

Furthermore, 33% of small firms raised prices over the last 3 months, the 3rd-highest reading since March 2023.

Meanwhile, 17% of business owners pointed to inflation as their single most important problem, up from 12% a year ago.

Small businesses are preparing for further price hikes as inflationary pressures mount.

US inflationary pressures are broadening:

Core CPI inflation surged to a 3-month annualized rate of +3.75% in October, its highest reading since April 2024.

This marks its 3rd consecutive monthly increase, up from +1.64% in July.

At the same time, core services less shelter inflation, also known as Supercore CPI and closely monitored by the Fed, rose to a 3-month annualized rate of +5.45%, its highest since mid-2024.

The weighted proportion of CPI components rising at an annualized rate above 2% soared to 76% last month, the largest percentage since August 2022.

This figure has risen +17 percentage points since July, marking its sharpest 3-month increase since early 2021.

The Fed's fight against inflation is far from over.
